units.zh: 卷九十二 遊俠傳第六十二
units.en: Volume 92: Biographies of the Knights-Errant (the sixty-second chapter).
units.literal: Volume 92: Biography of Wandering Knights, the sixty-second.

units.zh: 古者天子建國，諸侯立家，自卿、大夫以至於庶人，各有等差，是以民服事其上，而下無覬覦。
units.en: In the old order the Son of Heaven founded states, nobles founded lineages, and every rank from minister to peasant knew its place, so the people obeyed their betters and no underling nursed designs on his superior's seat.
units.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven established states, the feudal lords set up houses, from ministers and grandees down to commoners each had graded distinctions; therefore the people served those above them, and those below had no covetous designs.

units.zh: 孔子曰：「天下有道，政不在大夫。」
units.en: Confucius said, "When the Way holds sway, government does not rest with the ministers."
units.literal: Confucius said: "When the Way prevails in the world, government does not rest with the grandees."

units.zh: 百官有司奉法承令，以修所職，失職有誅，侵官有罰。
units.en: Every official followed statute and orders, did only the job assigned him, faced death for neglect, and fines for meddling outside his portfolio.
units.literal: The hundred offices and responsible officials uphold the law and receive orders, thereby cultivating their duties; for dereliction of duty there is execution, for encroaching on another's office there is punishment.

units.zh: 夫然，故上下相順，而庶事理焉。
units.en: Superiors and inferiors moved in step, and the business of the realm ran straight.
units.literal: Being thus, therefore above and below accorded with one another, and the affairs of the multitude were ordered.

units.zh: 周室既微，禮樂征伐自諸侯出。
units.en: Once Zhou grew weak, the feudal lords—not the king—set the tune for war and ceremony.
units.literal: When the Zhou house had already grown feeble, ritual, music, punishments, and expeditions issued from the feudal lords.

units.zh: 桓、文之後，大夫世權，陪臣執命。
units.en: After Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, ministers held hereditary sway and household stewards dictated policy.
units.literal: After Huan and Wen, grandees wielded hereditary power, and retainers grasped commands.

units.zh: 陵夷至於戰國，合從連衡，力政爭強。
units.en: By the Warring States era the realm had slid into leagues of north–south alliance and east–west deal-making, with every state flexing raw muscle.
units.literal: Declining onward to the Warring States, vertical alliances and horizontal pacts, rule by force vied for supremacy.

units.zh: 由是列國公子，魏有信陵、趙有平原、齊有孟嘗、楚有春申，皆借王公之勢，競為遊俠，雞鳴狗盜，無不賓禮。
units.en: Then came the famous lords of the blood: Xinling in Wei, Pingyuan in Zhao, Mengchang in Qi, and Chunshen in Chu. Trading on royal connections, they competed in knight-errantry and received even men of the pettiest talents as honored guests.
units.literal: Thereupon the noble sons of the states—Wei had Lord Xinling, Zhao Lord Pingyuan, Qi Lord Mengchang, Chu Lord Chunshen—all borrowed the power of kings and dukes, vied to be wandering knights, and cock-crow dog-thieves—none were not received with guest ritual.

units.zh: 而趙相虞卿棄國捐君，以周窮交魏齊之厄；
units.en: Minister Yu Qing of Zhao threw away office and ruler to ransom his ruined friend Wei Qi from disaster;
units.literal: Moreover Zhao's minister Yu Qing cast aside state and abandoned his lord, in order to deliver his destitute friend Wei Qi from peril;

units.zh: 信陵無忌竊符矯命，戮將專師，以赴平原之急：皆以取重諸侯，顯名天下，扼腕而游談者，以四豪為稱首。
units.en: Lord Xinling forged a royal order, killed a general, and seized an army to lift the siege on Pingyuan—all for the glamour of being indispensable to princes and famous across the world, so every bravo who cracked knuckles in a wine shop ranked the Four Lords first.
units.literal: Lord Xinling Wuji stole the tally and forged orders, executed a general and monopolized the army, to relieve Pingyuan's crisis—all thereby gained weight with the feudal lords and displayed their names under heaven; those who wrung wrists and roved in talk took the Four Heroes as their chief title.

units.zh: 於是背公死黨之議成，守職奉上之義廢矣。
units.en: Private loyalty trumped public duty, and the old ethic of serving one's post vanished.
units.literal: Thereupon the doctrine of turning backs on the public and dying for cliques was established, and the duty of guarding office and serving superiors was cast aside.

units.zh: 及至漢興，禁網疏闊，未之匡改也。
units.en: When the Han rose, the law stayed slack, and no one tightened it in time.
units.literal: Reaching to when Han arose, the prohibitory net was loose and wide, and it was not thereby corrected and reformed.

units.zh: 是故代相陳豨從車千乘，而吳濞、淮南皆招賓客以千數。
units.en: Hence Chen Xi, chancellor of Dai, rolled with a thousand chariots in his train, while Liu Pi in Wu and the king of Huainan each kept client armies counted in thousands.
units.literal: Therefore Chancellor Chen Xi of Dai had a thousand chariots following his carriage, while Liu Pi of Wu and the Prince of Huainan each recruited guests by the thousands.

units.zh: 外戚大臣魏其、武安之屬競逐於京師，布衣遊俠劇孟、郭解之徒馳騖於閭閻，權行州域，力折公侯。
units.en: Inside Chang'an the Dou and Tian factions jostled for power, while in the alleys bare-chested swordsmen like Ju Meng and Guo Xie built reputations that cowed nobles and bent whole commanderies.
units.literal: Affinal ministers such as Marquis Weiqi and Marquis Wu'an vied in pursuit at the capital; common-cloth wandering knights such as Ju Meng and Guo Xie raced in the lanes—their authority ran through provinces, their force bent marquises and dukes.

units.zh: 眾庶榮其名跡，覬而慕之。
units.en: Commoners gloried in their legends and ached to imitate them.
units.literal: The multitude honored their names and tracks, looked up to and admired them.

units.zh: 雖其陷於刑辟，自與殺身成名，若季路、仇牧，死而不悔也。
units.en: Even when the law caught them, they styled themselves martyrs like Zilu or Qiu Mu—ready to die unrepentant for a famous end.
units.literal: Although they fell into punishments and executions, they themselves aligned with killing the body to complete the name, like Jilu and Qiu Mu—dying without regret.

units.zh: 故曾子曰：「上失其道，民散久矣。」
units.en: Master Zeng warned, "When rulers stray from the Way, the people lose their moorings."
units.literal: Therefore Master Zeng said: "When those above lose the Way, the people have long been scattered."

units.zh: 非明王在上，視之以好惡，齊之以禮法，民曷由知禁而反正乎！
units.en: Without a clear-sighted sovereign to show what he honors and detests, and ritual and statute to snap them back into line, how will folk learn where the boundary lies?
units.literal: Unless an enlightened king is above, surveying them with likes and dislikes, aligning them with ritual and law, how can the people know prohibition and return to rectitude!

units.zh: 古之正法：五伯，三王之罪人也；
units.en: By ancient right standards the Five Hegemons were already traitors to the Three Sage-Kings;
units.literal: The correct law of antiquity: the Five Hegemons were criminals against the Three Kings;

units.zh: 而六國，五伯之罪人也。
units.en: the Six States were criminals against the Five Hegemons.
units.literal: and the Six States were criminals against the Five Hegemons.

units.zh: 夫四豪者，又六國之罪人也。
units.en: The Four Heroes were criminals against the Six States in turn.
units.literal: As for the Four Heroes, they were again criminals against the Six States.

units.zh: 況於郭解之倫，以匹夫之細，竊殺生之權，其罪已不容於誅矣。
units.en: How much less pardonable are commoners like Guo Xie who arrogate the power of life and death—no punishment could be enough.
units.literal: How much more men like Guo Xie, by the meanness of a common fellow, usurping the power over life and death—their guilt already brooked no room within execution.

units.zh: 觀其溫良泛愛，振窮周急，謙退不伐，亦皆有絕異之姿。
units.en: Yet watch them help the poor, soothe the desperate, and refuse praise—they could show a charisma few gentlemen matched.
units.literal: Observing their warmth and goodness, broad love, raising the destitute and relieving the urgent, modest retreat without boasting—they also all had surpassingly unusual bearing.

units.zh: 惜乎不入於道德，苟放縱於末流，殺身亡宗，非不幸也。
units.en: What a waste that they never steered that energy into true virtue, but rode the fad to ruin—death and lineage cut off were not accidents but the natural bill.
units.literal: It is regrettable that they did not enter into morality and virtue, but recklessly gave rein in the downstream current; killing the body and destroying the clan—this is not misfortune.

units.zh: 自魏其、武安、淮南之後，天子切齒，衛、霍改節。
units.en: After the Dou–Tian feud and the Huainan revolt, the emperor set his jaw, and even Wei Qing and Huo Qubing learned to keep clients at arm's length.
units.literal: After Weiqi, Wu'an, and Huainan, the Son of Heaven gnashed his teeth, and Wei and Huo changed their conduct.

units.zh: 然郡國豪桀處處各有，京師親戚冠蓋相望，亦古今常道，莫足言者。
units.en: Still, every province bred its bravos, and Chang'an kinfolk still jostled in official carriages—an old story, hardly worth another line.
units.literal: Yet in commanderies and kingdoms fierce champions existed everywhere; at the capital affinal kin and covered carriages looked upon one another—it is also the constant way of past and present, not worth speaking of.

units.zh: 唯成帝時，外家王氏賓客為盛，而樓護為帥。
units.en: Under Chengdi the Wang in-laws ran the richest salon of retainers, headed by Lou Hu.
units.literal: Only in Emperor Cheng's time, the Wang affinal family's guests were at their height, and Lou Hu was their leader.

units.zh: 及王莽時，諸公之間陳遵為雄，閭里之俠原涉為魁。
units.en: By Wang Mang's day Chen Zun lorded it among the great ministers, while Yuan She ruled the back-alley swordsmen.
units.literal: Reaching Wang Mang's time, among the various dukes Chen Zun was champion; among lane-knight-errants Yuan She was chief.

units.zh: 硃家，魯人，高祖同時也。
units.en: Zhu Jia of Lu was a man of Gaozu's generation.
units.literal: Zhu Jia was a man of Lu, contemporary with Gaozu.

units.zh: 魯人皆以儒教，而硃家用俠聞。
units.en: Lu was famous for scholars, yet the Zhu family made its name with swords.
units.literal: The people of Lu all took Confucian teaching, but the Zhu household became known by knight-errantry.

units.zh: 所臧活豪士以百數，其餘庸人不可勝言。
units.en: He saved hundreds of desperate fighting men and countless humbler souls besides.
units.literal: Those he harbored and kept alive as bold knights were in the hundreds; the remaining common people cannot be fully told.

units.zh: 然終不伐其能，飲其德，諸所嘗施，唯恐見之。
units.en: He never bragged of his power or waited for thanks, and he hid from everyone he had helped.
units.literal: Yet in the end he did not boast of his ability or drink in their gratitude; for all he had ever bestowed, he only feared being seen by them.

units.zh: 振人不贍，先從貧賤始。
units.en: When he handed out relief, the poorest got served first.
units.literal: In raising those who lacked sufficiency, he began first from the poor and base.

units.zh: 家亡余財，衣不兼采，食不重味，乘不過軥牛。
units.en: His house stayed bare: plain single-color robes, one dish to a meal, and travel no grander than an ox cart.
units.literal: The household had no surplus wealth; his clothes did not combine two colors; his food did not double flavors; his riding did not exceed a yoked ox.

units.zh: 專趨人之急，甚於己私。
units.en: He chased other people's crises harder than his own comfort.
units.literal: He devoted himself solely to rushing to others' emergencies, more than to his private concerns.

units.zh: 既陰脫季布之厄，及布尊貴，終身不見。
units.en: After smuggling Ji Bu out of danger, he never showed his face again—not even when Ji Bu rose to high office.
units.literal: Having secretly delivered Ji Bu from peril, when Ji Bu became honored and noble, to the end of his life he did not see him.

units.zh: 自關以東，莫不延頸願交。
units.en: East of Hangu every bravo strained to claim his friendship.
units.literal: From east of the pass, none did not crane their necks wishing to associate with him.

units.zh: 楚田仲以俠聞，父事硃家，自以為行弗及也。
units.en: Tian Zhong of Chu, famed as a knight, treated Zhu Jia like a father and admitted he could not match him.
units.literal: Tian Zhong of Chu was known by knight-errantry; serving Zhu Jia with a father's deference, he considered his own conduct not equal.

units.zh: 田仲死後，有劇孟。
units.en: After Tian Zhong died, Ju Meng came to the fore.
units.literal: After Tian Zhong died, there was Ju Meng.

units.zh: 劇孟者，洛陽人也。
units.en: Ju Meng came from Luoyang.
units.literal: Ju Meng was a man of Luoyang.

units.zh: 周人以商賈為資，劇孟以俠顯。
units.en: Where Zhou folk prided themselves on trade, Ju Meng made his name with a sword.
units.literal: The Zhou people took merchants and peddlers as their capital; Ju Meng displayed himself by knight-errantry.

units.zh: 吳、楚反時，條侯為太尉，乘傳東，將至河南，得劇孟，喜曰：「吳、楚舉大事而不求劇孟，吾知其無能為已。」
units.en: During the Rebellion of Seven States, Zhou Yafu rode east as Grand Commandant, picked up Ju Meng in Henan, and laughed with relief: "If Wu and Chu forgot to recruit Ju Meng, they have already lost."
units.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, Marquis Tiao was Grand Commandant; riding post east, about to reach Henan, he obtained Ju Meng and joyfully said: "Wu and Chu are undertaking a great affair yet do not seek Ju Meng—I know they can accomplish nothing."

units.zh: 天下騷動，大將軍得之若一敵國雲。
units.en: Amid the empire's turmoil, the Grand General's gaining Ju Meng was reckoned equivalent to securing the allegiance of an entire rival state.
units.literal: All under heaven was in turmoil; for the Grand General to obtain him was like gaining an enemy state.

units.zh: 劇孟行大類硃家，而好博，多少年之戲。
units.en: Ju Meng lived like Zhu Jia but loved dice and the games of the young.
units.literal: Ju Meng's conduct was greatly similar to Zhu Jia's, but he liked gambling—much youthful sport.

units.zh: 然孟母死，自遠方送喪蓋千乘。
units.en: When his mother died, a thousand chariots followed her bier from every corner of the realm.
units.literal: Yet when Ju Meng's mother died, those who came from afar to join the funeral numbered roughly a thousand chariot teams.

units.zh: 及孟死，家無十金之財。
units.en: When he died, his heirs could not scrape together ten catties of gold.
units.literal: When Meng died, the household had not the wealth of ten in gold.

units.zh: 而符離王孟，亦以俠稱江、淮之間。
units.en: Wang Meng of Fuli was another blade between the Yangzi and the Huai.
units.literal: Moreover Wang Meng of Fuli was also called a knight-errant between the Yangzi and Huai.

units.zh: 是時，濟南瞷氏、陳周膚亦以豪聞。
units.en: Around then the Jians of Jinan and Zhou Fu of Chen were feared as local tyrants.
units.literal: At this time the Jian clan of Jinan and Zhou Fu of Chen were also heard of as champions.

units.zh: 景帝聞之，使使盡誅此屬。
units.en: Emperor Jing sent agents to wipe out every one of those clans.
units.literal: When Emperor Jing heard of it, he sent envoys to execute all this sort to the last.

units.zh: 其後，代諸白、梁韓毋辟、陽翟薛況、陝寒孺，紛紛復出焉。
units.en: Soon enough new names surfaced—the Bai families of Dai, Han Wubi in Liang, Xue Kuang in Yangdi, Han Ru in Shan—each as bold as the last.
units.literal: Afterward the various Bai of Dai, Han Wubi of Liang, Xue Kuang of Yangdi, Han Ru of Shan—one after another reappeared.

units.zh: 郭解，河內軹人也，溫善相人許負外孫也。
units.en: Guo Xie of Zhi in Henei was the maternal grandson of Xu Fu, the famous face-reader from Wen.
units.literal: Guo Xie was a man of Zhi in Henei, maternal grandson of the physiognomist Xu Fu of Wen.

units.zh: 解父任俠，孝文時誅死。
units.en: His father had lived by the sword and died on the execution ground under Emperor Wen.
units.literal: Xie's father practiced knight-errantry; in Emperor Xiaowen's time he was executed to death.

units.zh: 解為人靜悍，不飲酒。
units.en: Guo Xie was soft-spoken and deadly sober.
units.literal: Xie as a person was quiet and fierce, and did not drink wine.

units.zh: 少時陰賊感概，不快意，所殺甚眾。
units.en: As a youth he nursed grudges in silence and left a long trail of corpses whenever he felt slighted.
units.literal: In youth he was secretly vicious and stirred by indignation; when displeased, those he killed were very many.

units.zh: 以軀借友報仇，臧命作奸剽攻，休乃鑄錢掘塚，不可勝數。
units.en: He lent his blade for friends' feuds, hid wanted men, led raids, and in quieter moments counterfeited cash and robbed graves—too often to count.
units.literal: Lending his body to friends to avenge wrongs, harboring fugitives, doing wickedness, raiding and attacking; in leisure then casting coin and digging tombs—beyond counting.

units.zh: 適有天幸，窘急常得脫，若遇赦。
units.en: Heaven smiled on him: every tight corner opened like a general pardon.
units.literal: He happened to have heaven's luck; in straits and urgency he constantly got away, as if meeting an amnesty.

units.zh: 及解年長，更折節為儉，以德報怨，厚施而薄望。
units.en: In middle age he curbed his temper, paid good for evil, gave liberally, and asked nothing back.
units.literal: When Xie grew older, he further bent his demeanor to frugality, repaid enmity with virtue, was generous in giving and slight in expectation.

units.zh: 然其自喜為俠益甚。
units.en: Yet he only relished the knight's role more fiercely.
units.literal: Yet he himself delighted in being a knight-errant all the more.

units.zh: 既已振人之命，不矜其功，其陰賊著於心本發於睚眥如故云。
units.en: He saved lives without crowing, but the old killer still lurked inside, ready to strike over a sideways glance.
units.literal: Having already saved people's lives, he did not boast of his merit; the secret viciousness lodged in his heart-root and issuing from the corner of the eye remained as before, it is said.

units.zh: 而少年慕其行，亦輒為報仇，不使知也。
units.en: Young blades who worshipped him settled scores on his behalf and never told him.
units.literal: And the youths admired his conduct, also always avenging wrongs for him without letting him know.

units.zh: 解姊子負解之勢，與人飲，使之釂，非其任，強灌之。
units.en: Guo Xie's nephew traded on his name, forced a drinking partner to empty his cup, and when the man faltered, held him down and poured liquor down his throat.
units.literal: Xie's elder sister's son relied on Xie's power; drinking with someone, he made him drain the cup; it was not within his capacity, and he forcibly poured it down.

units.zh: 人怒，刺殺解姊子，亡去。
units.en: The guest lost his temper, stabbed the nephew to death, and vanished.
units.literal: The man grew angry, stabbed and killed Xie's elder sister's son, and fled away.

units.zh: 解姊怒曰：「以翁伯時人殺吾子，賊不得！」
units.en: Guo Xie's sister raged, "When you still answered to the name Wengbo, no killer of my boy would have lived an hour!"
units.literal: Xie's elder sister angrily said: "In the days when Wengbo held sway, if someone killed my son, the culprit would not have escaped!"

units.zh: 棄其屍道旁，弗葬，欲以辱解。
units.en: His sister left the body in the ditch unburied to shame her brother into action.
units.literal: His sister cast aside the corpse by the roadside, not burying it, wishing thereby to humiliate Xie.

units.zh: 解使人微知賊處。
units.en: Guo Xie quietly traced the killer's hideout.
units.literal: Xie sent men secretly to learn the culprit's whereabouts.

units.zh: 賊窘自歸，具以實告解。
units.en: Cornered, the man gave himself up and confessed everything to Guo Xie.
units.literal: The culprit, pressed, surrendered himself and fully told the truth to Xie.

units.zh: 解曰：「公殺之當，吾兒不直。」
units.en: Guo Xie said, "You were right to kill him; my nephew was in the wrong."
units.literal: Xie said: "Sir, your killing him was proper; my nephew was not in the right."

units.zh: 遂去其賊，罪其姊子，收而葬之。
units.en: He dismissed the killer, blamed his nephew for the fight, and gave the body a decent burial.
units.literal: Thereupon he let the culprit go, blamed his elder sister's son, gathered him in and buried him.

units.zh: 諸公聞之，皆多解之義，益附焉。
units.en: The local notables praised his fairness and clung to him tighter than ever.
units.literal: When the gentlemen heard it, they all praised Xie's rightness and attached themselves the more.

units.zh: 解出，人皆避，有一人獨箕踞視之。
units.en: When Guo Xie walked abroad, crowds parted—except one lounger who sat sprawled and stared him down.
units.literal: When Xie went out, people all yielded the way; there was one man who alone sat with legs sprawled and looked at him.

units.zh: 解問其姓名，客欲殺之。
units.en: Guo Xie asked his name; his followers drew steel.
units.literal: Xie asked his name; retainers wished to kill him.

units.zh: 解曰：「居邑屋不見敬，是吾德不修也，彼何罪！」
units.en: Guo Xie stopped them: "If folk in my own town do not respect me, the fault is mine—what has he done!"
units.literal: Xie said: "Dwelling in a town house and not being shown respect—this means my virtue is not cultivated; what crime has he!"

units.zh: 乃陰請尉史曰：「是人吾所重，至踐更時脫之。」
units.en: He slipped the precinct clerk a word: "That man matters to me—scratch him from corvée rolls when his turn comes."
units.literal: Thereupon he secretly requested the clerk of the commandant: "This is a man I esteem; when it reaches his turn for corvée duty, release him."

units.zh: 每至直更，數過，吏弗求。
units.en: Month after month the man showed for night watch and was waved past while clerks looked the other way.
units.literal: Each time it reached his watch rotation, several times he passed, yet the clerks did not summon him.

units.zh: 怪之，問其故，解使脫之。
units.en: Puzzled, he pressed for an answer and learned Guo Xie had bought him free.
units.literal: He wondered at it and asked the reason; Xie had caused him to be released.

units.zh: 箕踞者乃肉袒謝罪。
units.en: The lounger stripped to the waist and begged forgiveness.
units.literal: The man who had sat with legs sprawled then bared his flesh and apologized for his crime.

units.zh: 少年聞之，愈益慕解之行。
units.en: The young blades heard the story and idolized him more than ever.
units.literal: When the youths heard it, they admired Xie's conduct all the more.

units.zh: 洛陽人有相仇者，邑中賢豪居間以十數，終不聽。
units.en: Two feuding Luoyang clans ignored a dozen local peacemakers.
units.literal: There were men of Luoyang who bore mutual enmity; worthy champions of the town mediated between them by the tens, yet in the end they would not listen.

units.zh: 客乃見解。
units.en: Finally they sent for Guo Xie.
units.literal: A guest thereupon visited Xie.

units.zh: 解夜見仇家，仇家曲聽。
units.en: Guo Xie called by night, and even the bitterest foe bent his ear.
units.literal: Xie by night visited the enemy households, and the enemy households bent to listen.

units.zh: 解謂仇家：「吾聞洛陽諸公在間，多不聽。
units.en: He told them, "Your Luoyang elders have pleaded with you for months and you ignored them.
units.literal: Xie said to the enemy households: "I have heard that the gentlemen of Luoyang who were mediating mostly were not heeded.

units.zh: 今子幸而聽解，解奈何從它縣奪人邑賢大夫權乎！」
units.en: Now you honor me by yielding—how could I steal the credit that belongs to your own town worthies!"
units.literal: Now you have fortunately listened to Xie—how could Xie usurp from another county the authority of worthy grandees of people's towns!"

units.zh: 乃夜去，不使人知，曰：「且毋庸，待我去，令洛陽豪居間乃聽。」
units.en: He slipped away before dawn and left word: "Pretend nothing happened until I am gone, then let your local heroes announce the truce as theirs."
units.literal: Thereupon he departed by night, not letting people know, saying: 'For the moment do not use it; wait until I have gone, and let Luoyang champions mediate—then listen.'"

units.zh: 解為人短小，恭儉，出未嘗有騎，不敢乘車入其縣庭。
units.en: Guo Xie was a slight, humble man who walked everywhere and would not drive a cart onto the magistrate's yard.
units.literal: Xie as a person was short and small, respectful and frugal; when he went out he never had riders, and did not dare ride a carriage into his county courtyard.

units.zh: 之旁郡國，為人請求事，事可出，出之；
units.en: In neighboring provinces he pled cases: if a door could be opened, he opened it;
units.literal: Going to neighboring commanderies and kingdoms, for people he requested matters—if a matter could be gotten out, he got it out;

units.zh: 不可者，各令厭其意，然後乃敢嘗酒食。
units.en: when he could not win a pardon, he brokered face-saving terms for both sides—only then would he touch wine or meat.
units.literal: for those that could not, he had each satisfy the other's intent, and only then dared taste wine and food.

units.zh: 諸公以此嚴重之，爭為用。
units.en: Notables stood in awe of that scruple and competed to do his errands.
units.literal: The gentlemen for this reason treated him with stern respect and vied to be used by him.

units.zh: 邑中少年及旁近縣豪夜半過門，常十餘車，請得解客舍養之。
units.en: Local youths and county bravos would roll up in a dozen carts after midnight, begging to put his guests up at their expense.
units.literal: Youths of the town and champions of neighboring counties, passing his gate at midnight, were often more than ten chariots, requesting to obtain Xie's guest lodgings and support him.

units.zh: 及徙豪茂陵也，解貧，不中訾。
units.en: When the court ordered rich families moved to Maoling, Guo Xie was too poor on paper to qualify.
units.literal: When the time came to relocate champions to Maoling, Xie was poor and did not meet the property assessment.

units.zh: 吏恐，不敢不徙。
units.en: The local clerks dared not exempt him for fear of higher wrath.
units.literal: The clerks feared and did not dare not relocate him.

units.zh: 衛將軍為言：「郭解家貧，不中徙。」
units.en: General Wei Qing pleaded, "Guo Xie is too poor to be on the removal list."
units.literal: General Wei spoke for him: "Guo Xie's household is poor; he does not meet relocation."

units.zh: 上曰：「解布衣，權至使將軍，此其家不貧！」
units.en: The emperor snapped, "A commoner who can move my general is not poor!"
units.literal: The sovereign said: "Xie is common cloth—his power reaches to making a general speak; this means his household is not poor!"

units.zh: 解徙，諸公送者出千餘萬。
units.en: When he was forced west, well-wishers showered him with more than ten million cash in parting gifts.
units.literal: Xie was relocated; those gentlemen who sent him off contributed over ten million.

units.zh: 軹人楊季主子為縣掾，隔之，解兄子斷楊掾頭。
units.en: Yang Jizhu's son, a county clerk, blocked the convoy, so Guo Xie's elder brother's son took the man's head.
units.literal: A son of Yang Jizhu of Zhi was a county clerk and blocked him; Xie's elder brother's son cut off Clerk Yang's head.

units.zh: 解入關，關中賢豪知與不知，聞聲爭交歡。
units.en: Once inside the pass every Guanzhong notable, stranger or friend, rushed to win his smile at the mere mention of his name.
units.literal: Xie entered the pass; within the pass worthy champions, whether they knew him or not, at hearing his name vied to associate in friendship.

units.zh: 邑人又殺楊季主，季主家上書人又殺闕下。
units.en: Locals murdered Yang Jizhu; when his kin sent a petitioner to the throne, someone cut the petitioner down on the palace steps.
units.literal: Townsmen again killed Yang Jizhu; Jizhu's family sent up a memorialist, and the memorialist was again killed below the palace gate.

units.zh: 上聞，乃下吏捕解。
units.en: The emperor heard and ordered Guo Xie's arrest.
units.literal: When the sovereign heard of it, thereupon he sent down clerks to arrest Xie.

units.zh: 解亡，置其母家室夏陽，身至臨晉。
units.en: Guo Xie ran, stashed his mother and kin in Xiayang, and slipped on alone to Linjin.
units.literal: Xie fled, placing his mother, family, and household at Xiayang; in person he reached Linjin.

units.zh: 臨晉籍少翁素不知解，因出關。
units.en: Ji Shao'weng of Linjin, a stranger to Guo Xie, smuggled him through the barrier.
units.literal: Ji Shao'weng of Linjin had never known Xie, yet thereby got him out of the pass.

units.zh: 籍少翁已出解，解傳太原，所過輒告主人處。
units.en: Once Ji Shao'weng had passed him through the barrier, Guo Xie sent word ahead through Taiyuan, telling every host where he would lodge.
units.literal: After Ji Shao'weng had gotten Xie out, Xie relayed through Taiyuan; wherever he passed he always informed his hosts of his whereabouts.

units.zh: 吏逐跡至籍少翁，少翁自殺，口絕。
units.en: The trail led the police to Ji Shao'weng, who killed himself to seal his lips.
units.literal: Clerks followed the trail to Ji Shao'weng; Shao'weng killed himself, cutting off the mouth.

units.zh: 久之得解，窮治所犯為，而解所殺，皆在赦前。
units.en: Eventually they took Guo Xie and combed his record—yet every homicide dated to before a general amnesty.
units.literal: After a long time they obtained Xie, exhaustively investigated what he had done wrong, but Xie's killings had all been before amnesties.

units.zh: 軹有儒生侍使者坐，客譽郭解，生曰：「解專以奸犯公法，何謂賢？」
units.en: At Zhi a pedant sitting with the imperial envoy heard a guest praise Guo Xie and snapped, "Guo Xie lives by breaking the law—what is worthy about that?"
units.literal: In Zhi there was a scholar serving at the envoy's session; a guest praised Guo Xie, and the scholar said: "Xie specializes in using wickedness to violate public law—what is called worthy?"

units.zh: 解客聞之，殺此生，斷舌。
units.en: One of Guo Xie's followers cut him down and took his tongue.
units.literal: Xie's guest heard it, killed this scholar, and cut out the tongue.

units.zh: 吏以責解，解實不知殺者，殺者亦竟莫知為誰。
units.en: Magistrates blamed Guo Xie, who swore he knew nothing, and no informer ever named the blade.
units.literal: The clerks held Xie to account; Xie truly did not know the killer, and the killer in the end also none knew who it was.

units.zh: 吏奏解無罪。
units.en: The local report cleared him.
units.literal: The clerks memorialized that Xie was without guilt.

units.zh: 御史大夫公孫弘議曰：「解布衣為任俠行權，以睚眥殺人，解不知，此罪甚於解知殺之。
units.en: Imperial Counselor Gongsun Hong argued, "A commoner who wields a lord's power so that men kill over a dirty look—even if he never gave the order—has committed a worse crime than murder itself.
units.literal: Imperial Counselor Gongsun Hong deliberated and said: "Xie, as a commoner, practices knight-errantry and wields power; over a sidelong glance someone kills—Xie does not know—this guilt is greater than if Xie had known the killing.

units.zh: 當大逆無道。」
units.en: He should be charged with the capital crime of great impiety and lawlessness."
units.literal: He should be charged with great impiety and lawlessness."

units.zh: 遂族解。
units.en: The court wiped out his whole lineage.
units.literal: Thereupon they exterminated Xie's clan.

units.zh: 自是之後，俠者極眾，而無足數者。
units.en: After that, bravos swarmed the empire, but few worth naming.
units.literal: From this time onward, those who were knights were extremely many, yet none worth counting.

units.zh: 然關中長安樊中子，槐裡趙王孫，長陵高公子，西河郭翁中，太原魯翁孺，臨淮兒長卿，東陽陳君孺，雖為俠而恂恂有退讓君子之風。
units.en: Still, men like Fan Zhongzi in Chang'an, Zhao Wangsun in Huaili, Gao Gongzi in Changling, Guo Wengzhong of Xihe, Lu Wengru in Taiyuan, Er Changqing in Linhuai, and Chen Junru in Dongyang wore the knight's label yet behaved with courteous restraint.
units.literal: Yet within the pass—Fan Zhongzi of Chang'an, Zhao Wangsun of Huaili, Gao Gongzi of Changling, Guo Wengzhong of Xihe, Lu Wengru of Taiyuan, Er Changqing of Linhuai, Chen Junru of Dongyang—though they were knights, they were modest and had the bearing of gentlemen who yield.

units.zh: 至若北道姚氏，西道諸杜，南道仇景，東道趙佗羽公子，南陽趙調之徒，盜跖而居民間者耳，曷足道哉！
units.en: As for the Yao gang on the northern road, the Du clans on the western, Qiu Jing in the south, the so-called Zhao Tuo princeling in the east, Zhao Diao in Nanyang—they were bandits in broad daylight, hardly worth ink.
units.literal: As for the Yao clan of the northern road, the various Du of the western road, Qiu Jing of the southern road, Zhao Tuoyu, courtesy Gongzi, of the eastern road, Zhao Diao of Nanyang, and their sort, they were mere Robber Zhis living among the people. How are they worth speaking of?

units.zh: 此乃鄉者硃家所羞也。
units.en: Zhu Jia of old would have blushed to share a sentence with them.
units.literal: This is what the Zhu Jia of former times would have been ashamed of.

units.zh: 萭章字子夏，長安人也。
units.en: Yu Zhang, styled Zixia, came from Chang'an.
units.literal: Yu Zhang, courtesy name Zixia, was a man of Chang'an.

units.zh: 長安熾盛，街閭各有豪俠，章在城西柳市，號曰「城西萭章子夏」。
units.en: Chang'an seethed with swagger, each ward its own swordsmen; Yu Zhang held Willow Market west of the walls and was known as "West-City Yu Zixia."
units.literal: Chang'an blazed with splendor; each street and ward had its fierce knights; Zhang was in Willow Market west of the city, styled "Yu Zhang Zixia of the west of the city."

units.zh: 為京兆尹門下督，從至殿中，侍中諸侯貴人爭欲揖章，莫與京兆尹言者。
units.en: As chief retainer to the Metropolitan Governor he entered the palace, where nobles and attendants crowded to bow to him and ignored their own superior.
units.literal: He was retainer overseer under the Metropolitan Governor; following into the palace hall, palace attendants, feudal lords, and nobles vied to bow to Zhang, and none spoke with the Metropolitan Governor.

units.zh: 章逡循甚懼。
units.en: Yu Zhang shrank back in terror.
units.literal: Zhang drew back in great fear.

units.zh: 其後京兆不復從也。
units.en: After that the governor never brought him inside again.
units.literal: Afterward the Metropolitan Governor did not again take him along.

units.zh: 與中書令石顯相善，亦得顯權力，門車常接轂。
units.en: He befriended Palace Secretary Shi Xian and borrowed the eunuch's clout until guest coaches jammed axle to axle at his gate.
units.literal: He was on good terms with Palace Secretary Shi Xian, and also obtained Shi's power; carriages at his gate constantly hub to hub.

units.zh: 至成帝初，石顯坐專權擅勢免官，徙歸故郡。
units.en: Early in Chengdi's reign Shi Xian lost his post for bullying the government and was banished home.
units.literal: Reaching the beginning of Emperor Cheng's reign, Shi Xian, sitting guilty of monopolizing authority and arrogating power, was dismissed from office and removed to his native commandery.

units.zh: 顯資巨萬，當去，留床席器物數百萬直，欲以與章，章不受。
units.en: Shi Xian was worth millions; on the road out he tried to deed Yu Zhang furniture and fittings valued in the millions, but Yu Zhang refused.
units.literal: Xian's assets were in the tens of millions; when about to depart, he left beds, mats, and utensils worth several million, wishing to give them to Zhang; Zhang did not accept.

units.zh: 賓客或問其故，章歎曰：「吾以布衣見哀於石君，石君家破，不能有以安也，而受其財物，此為石氏之禍，萭氏反當以為福邪！」
units.en: When retainers pressed him, Yu Zhang sighed, "Shi Xian pitied me when I was nobody; now his house is ruined and I cannot save him—if I grabbed his goods I would pile disaster on the Shis and call it luck for the Yus!"
units.literal: Guests some asked the reason; Zhang sighed and said: "I, in common cloth, was pitied by Lord Shi; Lord Shi's house is broken—I am unable to have means to settle him, yet accept his goods and wealth—this would be calamity for the Shi clan; would the Yu clan instead take it as fortune!"

units.zh: 諸公以是服而稱之。
units.en: Notables honored him for that scruple.
units.literal: The gentlemen for this reason admired and praised him.

units.zh: 河平中，王尊為京兆尹，捕擊豪俠，殺章及箭張回、酒市趙君都、賈子光，皆長安名豪，報仇怨養刺客者也。
units.en: Under Heping, Wang Zun as Metropolitan Governor swept the bravos: he executed Yu Zhang, the archer Zhang Hui, Zhao Jundu of Wine Market, and Jia Ziguang—Chang'an kingpins who kept killers on retainer.
units.literal: In the Heping era, Wang Zun was Metropolitan Governor; he arrested and struck down fierce knights, killing Zhang along with Zhang Hui "Arrow," Zhao Jundu of Wine Market, and Jia Ziguang—all were famous champions of Chang'an who avenged grudges and nurtured assassins.

units.zh: 樓護字君卿，齊人。
units.en: Lou Hu, styled Junqing, came from Qi.
units.literal: Lou Hu, courtesy name Junqing, was a man of Qi.

units.zh: 父世醫也，護少隨父為醫長安，出入貴戚家。
units.en: His father was a hereditary physician; Lou Hu grew up trailing him through the mansions of the great in Chang'an.
units.literal: His father for generations was a physician; Hu in youth followed his father practicing as a physician in Chang'an, going in and out of noble and affinal houses.

units.zh: 護誦醫經、本草、方術數十萬言，長者咸愛重之，共謂曰：「以君卿之材，何不宦學乎？」
units.en: He memorized hundreds of thousands of characters of pharmacopeia and case lore, and elders urged him, "A mind like yours belongs in office, not in an apothecary."
units.literal: Hu recited medical classics, materia medica, and formulas several hundred thousand characters; elders all loved and esteemed him, jointly saying to him: "With Junqing's talent, why not enter official learning?"

units.zh: 由是辭其父，學經傳，為京兆吏數年，甚得名譽。
units.en: So he quit medicine, mastered the canonical texts, spent years on the Metropolitan staff, and made a name.
units.literal: Thereupon he took leave of his father, studied Classics and commentaries, served as a Metropolitan clerk several years, and gained great reputation.

units.zh: 是時，王氏方盛，賓客滿門，五侯兄弟爭名，其客各有所厚，不得左右，唯護盡入其門，咸得其歡心。
units.en: The Wangs were at their zenith: each of the five brothers hoarded clients who would not cross to a rival house—except Lou Hu, who dined in every mansion and kept them all smiling.
units.literal: At this time the Wang clan was flourishing, guests filling their gates; the five marquises' brothers vied for fame, each house's clients having their particular allegiance so one could not serve both sides—only Hu entered all their gates and won everyone's heart.

units.zh: 結士大夫，無所不傾，其交長者，尤見親而敬，眾以是服。
units.en: He charmed every circle of scholar-officials, showed real deference to his seniors, and won universal respect.
units.literal: He bonded with gentry officeholders; there was none he did not sway; in associating with elders he was especially seen as intimate and respected—the crowd therefore submitted.

units.zh: 為人短小精辯，論議常依名節，聽之者皆竦。
units.en: He was small, quick-tongued, and anchored every argument in honor—listeners sat bolt upright.
units.literal: As a person he was short but keenly eloquent; in discourse he constantly relied on reputation and integrity, and listeners all stood awestruck.

units.zh: 與谷永俱為五侯上客，長安號曰「谷子雲筆札，樓君卿脣舌」，言其見信用也。
units.en: He and Gu Yong were chief clients of the five Wang marquises, and the capital joked, "Ziyun wields the brush; Junqing wields the tongue"—both men were indispensable.
units.literal: Together with Gu Yong he was senior guest to the five marquises; Chang'an called it "Gu Ziyun's brush and documents, Lou Junqing's lips and tongue"—meaning they were trusted.

units.zh: 母死，送葬者致車二三千兩，閭里歌之曰：「五侯治喪樓君卿。」
units.en: When his mother died, the mourners who escorted the burial brought two or three thousand carriages. The neighborhoods sang of it: "The five marquises arranged the funeral for Lou Junqing."
units.literal: When his mother died, those who sent off the funeral brought two or three thousand teams of carriages; the wards sang of it: "The five marquises managed the funeral for Lou Junqing."

units.zh: 久之，平阿侯舉護方正，為諫大夫，使郡國。
units.en: Marquis Ping'e eventually nominated him as a candidate of integrity; he became a remonstrance grandee and toured the provinces on imperial business.
units.literal: After a long time Marquis Ping'e recommended Hu as upright and direct; he became Grandee Remonstrant and was dispatched to commanderies and kingdoms.

units.zh: 護假貸，多持幣帛，過齊，上書求上先人塚，因會宗族故人，各以親疏與束帛，一日數百金之費。
units.en: He borrowed heavily, loaded up with silk, detoured through Qi to petition at the ancestral tombs, feasted every kinsman and crony, and handed out silk by rank—burning hundreds of gold in a day.
units.literal: Hu borrowed loans, holding much silk cash; passing through Qi, he memorialized asking permission to visit his ancestors' graves; thereby gathering kin and old friends, according to closeness each receiving a bundle of silk—expenses of several hundred gold in a single day.

units.zh: 使還，奏事稱意，擢為天水太守。
units.en: His tour report pleased the throne, and he was jumped up to governor of Tianshui.
units.literal: When he returned from mission and reported to satisfaction, he was promoted to governor of Tianshui.

units.zh: 數歲免，家長安中。
units.en: A few years later he was cashiered and settled again in the capital.
units.literal: Several years later dismissed, he dwelt in Chang'an.

units.zh: 時成都侯商為大司馬衛將軍，罷朝，欲候護，其主簿諫：「將軍至尊，不宜入閭巷。」
units.en: At the time Wang Shang, Marquis of Chengdu, was Grand Marshal and General of the Guards. After leaving court, he wanted to call on Lou Hu, but his chief clerk remonstrated, "Your rank is supremely exalted; you should not enter common lanes and alleys."
units.literal: At the time Marquis Chengdu Wang Shang was Grand Marshal and Guards General; leaving court he wished to call on Hu. His chief clerk remonstrated: "The general is most exalted; he should not enter lanes."

units.zh: 商不聽，遂往至護家。
units.en: Wang Shang ignored the advice and rolled up to Lou Hu's door.
units.literal: Shang did not listen and went on to reach Hu's house.

units.zh: 家狹小，官屬立車下，久住移時，天欲雨，主簿謂西曹諸掾曰：「不肯強諫，反雨立閭巷！」
units.en: The cottage was tiny, so the escort froze under their axles while rain threatened; the chief clerk hissed at the western staff, "No strong warning—now we soak in an alley!"
units.literal: The house was narrow; officials stood beneath their chariots a long time; the sky was about to rain. The chief clerk said to the western bureau clerks: "You would not forcefully remonstrate—instead we stand in the rain in an alley!"

units.zh: 商還，或白主簿語，商恨，以他職事去主簿，終身廢錮。
units.en: When Wang Shang heard the clerk's gibe on his return, he dismissed him on a trumped-up charge and barred him from office for life.
units.literal: When Shang returned, someone reported the chief clerk's words; Shang resented it and removed the chief clerk on another official matter, consigning him to lifelong disqualification.

units.zh: 後護復以薦為廣漢太守。
units.en: Later a nomination made him governor of Guanghan.
units.literal: Later Hu again by recommendation became governor of Guanghan.

units.zh: 元始中，王莽為安漢公，專政，莽長子宇與妻兄呂寬謀以血塗莽第門，欲懼莽令歸政。
units.en: In the Yuan shi years Wang Mang ruled as Lord of Anhan while his heir Wang Yu and brother-in-law Lü Kuan smeared blood on the mansion gate hoping to scare him into yielding power.
units.literal: In the Yuan shi era, Wang Mang was Lord of Anhan and monopolized government; Mang's eldest son Yu with his wife's elder brother Lü Kuan plotted to smear blood on Mang's gate, wishing to frighten Mang into returning the government.

units.zh: 發覺，莽大怒，殺宇，而呂寬亡。
units.en: The plot surfaced; Mang executed his own son while Lü Kuan ran.
units.literal: When it was discovered, Mang was greatly angry, killed Yu, while Lü Kuan fled.

units.zh: 寬父素與護相知，寬至廣漢過護，不以事實語也。
units.en: Lü Kuan's father was an old friend of Lou Hu's; the fugitive called on him in Guanghan but never breathed a word of the conspiracy.
units.literal: Kuan's father had long been acquainted with Hu; when Kuan reached Guanghan he visited Hu, but did not tell him the facts of the matter.

units.zh: 到數日，名捕寬詔書至，護執寬。
units.en: Within days the empire-wide warrant arrived, and Lou Hu handed Lü Kuan over.
units.literal: Several days after arriving, the edict for named arrest of Kuan arrived; Hu seized Kuan.

units.zh: 莽大喜，徵護入為前煇光，封息鄉侯，列於九卿。
units.en: Wang Mang was delighted, recalled Lou Hu to govern Qianhuiguang Commandery, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xixiang, and ranked him among the Nine Ministers.
units.literal: Mang was greatly pleased, summoned Hu to govern Qianhuiguang Commandery, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xixiang, and ranked him among the Nine Ministers.

units.zh: 莽居攝，槐里大賊趙朋、霍鴻等群起，延入前煇光界，護坐免為庶人。
units.en: During Mang's regency, the Huaili rebels Zhao Peng and Huo Hong rose in force and spread into Qianhuiguang Commandery; Lou Hu was held responsible, dismissed, and reduced to commoner status.
units.literal: When Mang held the regency, great bandits of Huaili such as Zhao Peng and Huo Hong rose in groups and spread into the territory of Qianhuiguang Commandery; Hu was held responsible, dismissed, and reduced to commoner status.

units.zh: 其居位，爵祿賂遺所得亦緣手盡。
units.en: Every salary and gift he ever drew slipped through his fingers as fast as it came.
units.literal: While he held office, what rank emoluments and bribe-gifts yielded likewise passed through his hands to exhaustion.

units.zh: 既退居里巷，時五侯皆已死，年老失勢，賓客益衰。
units.en: Back in the alleys, the five Wang patrons dead and his own vigor gone, his salon thinned to a whisper.
units.literal: Having retired to lanes and wards, at the time the five marquises had all died; old in years and having lost power, his guests grew ever fewer.

units.zh: 至王莽篡位，以舊恩召見護，封為樓舊裡附城。
units.en: When Wang Mang seized the throne he remembered old ties, summoned Lou Hu, and enfeoffed him as a minor attached-city noble at Loujiuli.
units.literal: Reaching Wang Mang's usurpation of the throne, by old favor he summoned and saw Hu, enfeoffing him as attached city lord of Loujiuli.

units.zh: 而成都侯商子邑為大司空，貴重，商故人皆敬事邑，唯護自安如舊節，邑亦父事之，不敢有闕。
units.en: Wang Yi, Wang Shang's son, became Grand Minister of Works; every old friend flattered him—except Lou Hu, who kept the easy equality of earlier days, so Yi treated him like a father and never slipped in courtesy.
units.literal: Moreover the Chengdu Marquis Shang's son Yi was Grand Minister of Works, honored and weighty; Shang's old acquaintances all respectfully served Yi—only Hu rested easy as in former propriety, and Yi also served him with father's deference, not daring to be deficient.

units.zh: 時請召賓客，邑居樽下，稱「賤子上壽」。
units.en: At feasts Wang Yi took the seat below the wine jar and toasted him as "your humble son."
units.literal: When he invited and summoned guests, Yi sat below the wine goblet, calling himself "your worthless son offering longevity."

units.zh: 坐者百數，皆離席伏，護獨東鄉正坐，字謂邑曰：「公子貴如何！」
units.en: A hundred guests dropped to the kowtow while Lou Hu alone sat facing east and drawled, "Well, Yi—how does it feel to be the great man?"
units.literal: Hundreds were seated there. All left their mats and prostrated themselves, but Hu alone remained sitting upright, facing east, and addressed Yi familiarly: "How does the young lord enjoy his eminence?"

units.zh: 初，護有故人呂公，無子，歸護。
units.en: Long before, a childless friend surnamed Lü had moved in with him.
units.literal: At first Hu had an old friend Lord Lü, without sons, who entrusted himself to Hu.

units.zh: 護身與呂公、妻與呂嫗同食。
units.en: He and his wife shared table and board with the old couple.
units.literal: Hu in person with Lord Lü, and his wife with Old Lady Lü, ate together.

units.zh: 及護家居，妻子頗厭呂公。
units.en: Once Lou Hu retired, his wife and children grew tired of the guests.
units.literal: When Hu dwelt at home, wife and children somewhat wearied of Lord Lü.

units.zh: 護聞之，流涕責其妻子曰：「呂公以故舊窮老托身於我，義所當奉。」
units.en: Lou Hu wept and scolded his household: "Lord Lü is a ruined old friend who threw himself on my mercy—duty says I keep him."
units.literal: When Hu heard it, weeping he rebuked his wife and children, saying: "Lord Lü, as an old friend poor and old, entrusted his body to me—it is rightness that I should support him."

units.zh: 遂養呂公終身。
units.en: He fed the couple until they died.
units.literal: Thereupon he supported Lord Lü to the end of his life.

units.zh: 護卒，子嗣其爵。
units.en: When Lou Hu died, his son inherited the fief.
units.literal: When Hu died, his son inherited his noble rank.

units.zh: 陳遵字孟公，杜陵人也。
units.en: Chen Zun, styled Menggong, came from Duling.
units.literal: Chen Zun, courtesy Menggong, was a man of Duling.

units.zh: 祖父遂，字長子，宣帝微時與有故，相隨博弈，數負進。
units.en: His grandfather Sui, styled Zhangzi, had known the future Emperor Xuan in his obscure days; they gambled together, and Sui often lost.
units.literal: His grandfather Sui, courtesy Zhangzi, had old ties with the future Emperor Xuan when he was still obscure; they gambled together, and Sui often lost.

units.zh: 及宣帝即位，用遂，稍遷至太原太守，乃賜遂璽書曰：「制詔太原太守：官尊祿厚，可以償博進矣。
units.en: When Xuan took the throne he employed Sui, who rose to Grand Administrator of Taiyuan. The emperor sent him a sealed edict: "To the Grand Administrator of Taiyuan: your rank is high and your pay ample—you can repay your gambling losses.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he employed Sui, who gradually rose to Grand Administrator of Taiyuan. The emperor then bestowed on Sui an imperial edict saying, "By decree to the Grand Administrator of Taiyuan: your office is high and your salary ample—you can repay your gambling losses.

units.zh: 妻君寧時在旁，知狀。」
units.en: Your wife Jun Ning was there and knows the whole story."
units.literal: Your wife Jun Ning was present at the time and knows the circumstances."

units.zh: 遂於是辭謝，因曰：「事在元平元年赦令前。」
units.en: Sui thanked him and replied, "That happened before the Yuanping amnesty of the first year."
units.literal: Sui then declined with thanks and added, "The matter fell before the Yuanping first-year amnesty."

units.zh: 其見厚如此。
units.en: That was how highly he was favored.
units.literal: Such was the favor shown him.

units.zh: 元帝時，徵遂為京兆尹，至廷尉。
units.en: Under Emperor Yuan, Sui was called up as Metropolitan Governor and rose to Commandant of Justice.
units.literal: Under Emperor Yuan, Sui was summoned as Metropolitan Governor and reached the post of Commandant of Justice.

units.zh: 遵少孤，與張竦伯松俱為京兆史。
units.en: Orphaned young, Chen Zun served as a clerk in the Metropolitan District alongside Zhang Song, courtesy name Bosong.
units.literal: Zun in youth was orphaned; together with Zhang Song courtesy Bosong he was a Metropolitan clerk.

units.zh: 竦博學通達，以廉儉自守，而遵放縱不拘，操行雖異，然相親友，哀帝之末俱著名字，為後進冠。
units.en: Zhang Song was bookish and abstemious; Chen Zun was a rake—opposites who stayed fast friends and, by Aidi's end, topped every young blade's list.
units.literal: Song was broadly learned and penetrating, guarding himself with integrity and frugality, while Zun was unrestrained and not bound; though their conduct differed, yet they were intimate friends; at the end of Emperor Ai both had famous names, crowning the younger set.

units.zh: 並入公府，公府掾史率皆羸車小馬，不上鮮明，而遵獨極輿馬衣服之好，門外車騎交錯。
units.en: They joined a minister's staff where everyone else rattled up in patched carts—Chen Zun alone rolled in matched teams and silks until his gate looked like a parade ground.
units.literal: Together they entered the ducal mansion; ducal mansion clerks generally all had lean carts and small horses, not rising to splendor, but Zun alone exhausted the excellence of carriages, horses, and clothing; outside his gate chariots and riders crisscrossed.

units.zh: 又日出醉歸，曹事數廢。
units.en: He drank from dawn to stupor and let paperwork pile up.
units.literal: Moreover each day he went out drunk and returned; bureau business was repeatedly neglected.

units.zh: 西曹以故事適之，侍曹輒詣寺捨白遵曰：「陳卿今日以某事適。」
units.en: The western office docked his pay by rule; runners tracked him to his lodgings: "Sir, today's fine is for such-and-such."
units.literal: The western bureau by precedent fined him; the attendant bureau always went to the hostel and reported to Zun: "Lord Chen today was fined for such-and-such a matter."

units.zh: 遵曰：「滿百乃相聞。」
units.en: Chen Zun said, "Wake me when the tally hits a hundred."
units.literal: Zun said: "Only when it reaches a hundred then inform me."

units.zh: 故事，有百適者斥，滿百，西曹白請斥。
units.en: Regulations said a hundred demerits meant expulsion; at the hundredth mark the western bureau filed to fire him.
units.literal: By precedent, one who had a hundred fines was dismissed; when it reached a hundred, the western bureau reported requesting dismissal."

units.zh: 大司徒馬宮大儒優士，又重遵，謂西曹：「此人大度士，奈何以小文責之？」
units.en: Grand Minister Ma Gong, a Confucian who prized talent, told the western bureau, "Chen Zun is a big spirit—do not nag him over trivia."
units.literal: Grand Minister of Education Ma Gong, a great scholar who honored knights, also esteemed Zun, saying to the western bureau: "This man is a large-minded gentleman—how can you hold him to petty paperwork?"

units.zh: 乃舉遵能治三輔劇縣，補郁夷令。
units.en: So he nominated Chen Zun for a tough county in the capital region and got him posted to Yuyi.
units.literal: Thereupon he recommended Zun as able to govern a difficult county of the Three Adjuncts, appointing him magistrate of Yuyi.

units.zh: 久之，與扶風相失，自免去。
units.en: He later quarreled with the Fufeng chancellor and resigned on his own.
units.literal: After a long time, having fallen out with the Fufeng chancellor, he removed himself from office.

units.zh: 槐裡大賊趙朋、霍鴻等起，遵為校尉，擊朋、鴻有功，封嘉威侯。
units.en: When Zhao Peng and Huo Hong raided Huaili, Chen Zun led a column, crushed them, and earned the marquisate of Jiawei.
units.literal: Great bandits of Huaili such as Zhao Peng and Huo Hong rose; Zun was colonel, struck Peng and Hong with merit, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Jiawei.

units.zh: 居長安中，列侯近臣貴戚皆貴重之。
units.en: Back in Chang'an every marquis and in-law treated him as royalty.
units.literal: Dwelling in Chang'an, ranked marquises, close ministers, and noble affines all honored him as weighty.

units.zh: 牧守當之官，及郡國豪桀至京師者，莫不相因到遵門。
units.en: Every governor bound for a post and every provincial bravo who hit the capital made Chen Zun's house their first stop.
units.literal: Governors about to take office, and champions of commanderies and kingdoms who reached the capital—none did not take the occasion to arrive at Zun's gate.

units.zh: 遵嗜酒，每大飲，賓客滿堂，輒關門，取客車轄投井中，雖有急，終不得去。
units.en: Chen Zun loved banquets: once the hall filled he barred the doors and dropped the guests' axle pins down the well so no emergency could pry them loose.
units.literal: Zun was addicted to wine; whenever he drank heavily, guests filling the hall, he would shut the gate, take the guests' carriage linchpins and throw them in the well—though there was urgency, in the end they could not leave.

units.zh: 嘗有部刺史奏事，過遵，值其方飲，刺史大窮，候遵沾醉時，突入見遵母，叩頭自白當對尚書有期會狀，母乃令從後閣出去。
units.en: A provincial inspector once stopped at Chen Zun's residence while on his way to report to the Secretariat, only to find a drinking party in progress. Hard pressed for time, he waited until Zun was thoroughly drunk, forced his way in to see Zun's mother, kowtowed, and explained his deadline. She then had him led out through a rear passage.
units.literal: Once there was a regional inspector reporting on affairs; passing Zun's place he encountered him just drinking—the inspector was greatly pressed; waiting until Zun was soaked in drunk, he burst in to see Zun's mother, knocked his head and himself explained that he had a scheduled meeting to answer the Imperial Secretary; the mother then ordered him to go out through the rear passage.

units.zh: 遵大率常醉，然事亦不廢。
units.en: He was almost always drunk—yet the desk work still got done.
units.literal: Zun for the most part was constantly drunk, yet affairs were also not abandoned.

units.zh: 長八尺餘，長頭大鼻，容貌甚偉。
units.en: He stood over eight feet, with a long head, big nose, and a commanding frame.
units.literal: He was over eight chi in height, long-headed and large-nosed, his bearing very imposing.

units.zh: 略涉傳記，贍於文辭。
units.en: He had read widely and wrote with flair.
units.literal: He broadly perused records and biographies, and was ample in literary phrasing.

units.zh: 性善書，與人尺牘，主皆藏去以為榮。
units.en: His calligraphy was prized; hosts framed his notes as trophies.
units.literal: By nature skilled at writing, when he gave people letters, hosts all treasured and put them away as honor.

units.zh: 請求不敢逆，所到，衣冠懷之，唯恐在後。
units.en: No favor asked was refused; everywhere the elite courted him for fear of missing his notice.
units.literal: Requests he did not dare refuse; wherever he arrived, gentry cherished him, only fearing to be behind.

units.zh: 時列侯有與遵同姓字者，每至人門，曰陳孟公，坐中莫不震動，既至而非，因號其人曰陳驚坐雲。
units.en: Another marquis bore the same surname and courtesy name. Whenever he announced himself at someone's gate as Chen Menggong, everyone within started in excitement, only to be disappointed when the visitor proved not to be Chen Zun. They therefore dubbed him Chen Who Startles the Company.
units.literal: At the time there was a ranked marquis who shared Zun's surname and personal name; whenever he reached someone's gate and said "Chen Menggong," none seated did not tremble with shock; when he arrived and it was not the right man, therefore they styled that man "Chen Startle-the-Seats," it is said.

units.zh: 王莽素奇遵材，在位多稱譽者，由是起為河南太守。
units.en: Wang Mang admired his gifts; enough officials sang his praise that he was named governor of Henan.
units.literal: Wang Mang had always marveled at Zun's talent; many in office praised him; thereby he was raised to be governor of Henan.

units.zh: 既至官，當遣從史西，召善書吏十人於前，治私書謝京師故人。
units.en: On his first day he lined up ten copyists and dictated hundreds of thank-you notes to Chang'an friends.
units.literal: Having reached office, when about to dispatch following clerks west, he summoned ten skilled scribes before him and composed private letters thanking old friends of the capital.

units.zh: 遵馮幾，口占書吏，且省官事，書數百封，親疏各有意，河南大驚。
units.en: He leaned on the desk, dictated mail while signing documents, tailored every letter to its recipient, and left Henan clerks gaping.
units.literal: Zun leaned on the armrest, orally dictating to the scribes, and at the same time reviewing official business; he wrote several hundred letters, close and distant each having its intent—Henan was greatly astonished.

units.zh: 數月免。
units.en: Within months he was sacked again.
units.literal: Several months later he was dismissed.

units.zh: 初，遵為河南太守，而弟級為荊州牧，當之官，俱過長安富人故淮陽王外家左氏飲食作樂。
units.en: While Chen Zun governed Henan and his brother Chen Ji was taking up the Jingzhou shepherdship, both detoured to party at the Chang'an villa of the Zuo clan—rich in-laws of the late King of Huaiyang.
units.literal: At first, when Zun was governor of Henan and his younger brother Ji was shepherd of Jingzhou, about to take office, together they passed the house of the wealthy former King of Huaiyang's maternal kin, the Zuo clan of Chang'an, eating, drinking, and making merry.

units.zh: 後司直陳崇聞之，劾奏：「遵兄弟幸得蒙恩超等歷位，遵爵列侯，備郡守，級州牧奉使，皆以舉直察枉宣揚聖化為職，不正身自慎。
units.en: Director Chen Chong impeached them: "These brothers owe their rapid rise to imperial favor—one a marquis and governor, the other a regional shepherd—yet they refuse the sober bearing their offices demand.
units.literal: Later Director of Integrity Chen Chong heard of it and impeached: "The Zun brothers have fortunately received grace beyond their rank in successive offices; Zun's noble rank is ranked marquis, filling governorship; Ji's shepherdship bears commission—all take promoting the straight and investigating the crooked and proclaiming sagely transformation as their duty, yet do not correct their persons and be cautious.

units.zh: 始遵初除，乘籓車入閭巷，過寡婦左阿君置酒歌謳，遵起舞跳梁，頓僕坐上，暮因留宿，為侍婢扶臥。
units.en: Soon after taking office, Chen Zun rode a screened carriage into the lanes and called on the widow Zuo Ajun, where wine was served and songs were sung. He rose to dance and caper, collapsed drunk at the gathering, stayed the night, and had her maids help him to bed.
units.literal: From the start, when Zun was first appointed, riding a screened cart into a lane, passing the widow Zuo Ajun he set wine and songs; Zun rose and danced, leaping the beam, collapsing drunk on the seat; at dusk therefore he stayed overnight, and serving maids helped him lie down.

units.zh: 遵知飲酒飫宴有節，禮不入寡婦之門，而湛酒混餚，亂男女之別，輕辱爵位，羞污印□，惡不可忍聞。
units.en: He knows ritual forbids carousing in a widow's house, yet he drowned in wine, blurred the sexes, insulted his commission, and smeared the seal—conduct too foul to repeat.
units.literal: Zun knows that drinking and feasting have their measure, and ritual does not enter a widow's gate, yet he sinks in wine and mingles dishes, confuses the separation of male and female, lightly insults noble rank, shames and defiles the seal (text damaged)—evil unbearable to hear.

units.zh: 臣請皆免。」
units.en: I ask that both be stripped of office."
units.literal: Your subject requests that both be dismissed."

units.zh: 遵既免，歸長安，賓客愈盛，飲食自若。
units.en: Both men were cashiered, yet Chen Zun's parties in Chang'an only grew wilder.
units.literal: After Zun was dismissed, returning to Chang'an, his guests grew even more numerous, and drinking and eating continued as before.

units.zh: 久之，復為九江及河內都尉，凡三為二千石。
units.en: Years later he served as chief commandant in Jiujiang and Henei—three stints at two-thousand-bushel rank.
units.literal: After a long time, he again became chief commandant of Jiujiang and of Henei; in all he thrice held two-thousand-shi rank.

units.zh: 而張竦亦至丹陽太守，封淑德侯。
units.en: Zhang Song meanwhile rose to governor of Danyang and the marquisate of Shude.
units.literal: And Zhang Song also reached governor of Danyang, enfeoffed as marquis of Shude.

units.zh: 後俱免官，以列侯歸長安。
units.en: Eventually both lost their posts and came home to Chang'an as titled nobles.
units.literal: Later both were dismissed from office, returning to Chang'an as ranked marquises.

units.zh: 竦居貧，無賓客，時時好事者從之質疑問事，論道經書而已。
units.en: Zhang Song lived poor and alone except when curious visitors dropped by to debate the canon.
units.literal: Song dwelt in poverty, without guests; from time to time those fond of affairs followed him to question doubtful matters, discussing the Way and Classics only.

units.zh: 而遵晝夜呼號，車騎滿門，酒肉相屬。
units.en: Chen Zun howled night and day, jammed his gate with carriages, and stacked feast on feast.
units.literal: But Zun day and night shouted and called; chariots and riders filled his gate; wine and meat followed one another.

units.zh: 先是，黃門郎揚雄作《酒箴》以諷諫成帝，其文為酒客難法度士，譬之於物，曰：「子猶瓶矣。
units.en: Earlier Yang Xiong had written his Wine Admonition for Chengdi—a drunk lecturing a prig: "You are the pottery jar.
units.literal: Earlier, Palace Attendant Yang Xiong composed the "Wine Admonition" to remonstrate Emperor Cheng; its text had a wine guest rebuke a man of law and measure, comparing him to a thing, saying: "You are like a jar.

units.zh: 觀瓶之居，居井之眉，處高臨深，動常近危。
units.en: Look at the jar on the well curb—perched high over a fatal drop, every shift nearly a spill.
units.literal: Observe the jar's dwelling: it dwells on the brow of the well, occupying height and overlooking depth; in movement it constantly nears peril.

units.zh: 酒醪不入口，臧水滿懷，不得左右，牽於纆徽。
units.en: No wine ever wets its lips, yet it hoards the whole well; it cannot roll, only hangs on its hawser.
units.literal: Wine mash does not enter the mouth; stored water fills the bosom; it cannot move left or right, hauled by ropes and cords.

units.zh: 一旦叀礙，為瓽所轠，身提黃泉，骨肉為泥。
units.en: One slip of the rope and the jar shatters in the shaft—down you go, nothing left but mud.
units.literal: If once blocked and obstructed, it is crushed by the well-brick; the body is lifted to the Yellow Springs, flesh and bone become mud.

units.zh: 自用如此，不如鴟夷。
units.en: Better the wandering wineskin than that brittle pride.
units.literal: To be used thus is not as good as the leather wine-bag.

units.zh: 鴟夷滑稽，腹如大壺，盡日盛酒，人復借酤。
units.en: The wineskin is supple as a belly-jar, holds liquor all day, and goes out on loan to every tavern.
units.literal: The leather bag is nimble and slick; its belly is like a great jar, all day holding wine, and people again borrow to buy drink.

units.zh: 常為國器，托於屬車，出入兩宮，經營公家。
units.en: It rides the imperial baggage train, passes both palaces, and runs the court business—true state gear.
units.literal: It always serves as state vessel, entrusted to the attendant train, entering and leaving the two palaces, managing the public house.

units.zh: 繇是言之，酒何過乎！」
units.en: Tell me again how wine is the villain!"
units.literal: Speaking from this, what fault has wine!"

units.zh: 遵大喜之，常謂張竦：「吾與爾猶是矣。
units.en: Chen Zun loved the parable and told Zhang Song, "That wineskin is you and me.
units.literal: Zun greatly delighted in it, often saying to Zhang Song: "You and I are just like this.

units.zh: 足下諷誦經書，苦身自約，不敢差跌，而我放意自恣，浮湛俗間，官爵功名，不減於子，而差獨樂，顧不優邪！」
units.en: You grind through the canon and watch every step; I drift through the world drunk—yet my titles match yours and I have twice the fun. Who is ahead?"
units.literal: You chant the Classics, torment your body with self-restraint, dare not stumble, while I give rein to my will and indulge myself, floating and sinking in the vulgar world—office, noble rank, and fame are not less than yours, yet I enjoy a surplus of pleasure—is that not better!"

units.zh: 竦曰：「人各有性，長短自裁。
units.en: Zhang Song answered, "Nature sets each man his span.
units.literal: Song said: "Each man has his nature; long and short he cuts for himself.

units.zh: 子欲為我亦不能，吾而效子亦敗矣。
units.en: You could not live my life, nor I yours without ruin.
units.literal: If you wished to be me you could not; if I imitated you I would also fail.

units.zh: 雖然，學我者易持，效子者難將，吾常道也。」
units.en: Still, my disciples stay steady; yours would break the reins—that is my proverb."
units.literal: Even so, those who study me are easy to hold; those who imitate you are hard to lead—this is my constant saying."

units.zh: 及王莽敗，二人俱客於池陽，竦為賊兵所殺。
units.en: When Wang Mang fell they fled to Chiyang, where bandits cut down Zhang Song.
units.literal: When Wang Mang fell, both men were guests at Chiyang; Song was killed by rebel troops.

units.zh: 更始至長安，大臣薦遵為大司馬護軍，與歸德侯劉颯俱使匈奴。
units.en: Gengshi's court named Chen Zun marshal-guard to the Grand Marshal and sent him with Liu Sa of Guide marquisate as envoys to the shanyu.
units.literal: When Gengshi reached Chang'an, great ministers recommended Zun as marshal of the Grand Marshal's guard; together with Marquis Guide Liu Sa he was sent to the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 單于欲脅詘遵，遵陳利害，為言曲直，單于大奇之，遣還。
units.en: The shanyu tried to break him; Chen Zun laid out every consequence until the ruler admired his nerve and sent him home.
units.literal: The chanyu wished to coerce and humiliate Zun; Zun set forth benefit and harm, speaking for him of crooked and straight; the chanyu marveled greatly at him and sent him back.

units.zh: 會更始敗，遵留朔方，為賊所敗，時醉見殺。
units.en: When Gengshi collapsed Chen Zun stayed north, was overrun by raiders, and died drunk in the melee.
units.literal: It happened that Gengshi fell; Zun remained at Shuofang, was defeated by bandits, and at the time drunk was killed.

units.zh: 原涉字巨先。
units.en: Yuan She, styled Juxian.
units.literal: Yuan She, courtesy name Juxian.

units.zh: 祖父武帝時以豪桀自陽翟徙茂陵。
units.en: His grandfather, a noted bravo, was resettled from Yangzhai to Maoling under Emperor Wu.
units.literal: His grandfather in Emperor Wu's time, as a fierce champion, was moved from Yangzhai to Maoling.

units.zh: 涉父哀帝時為南陽太守。
units.en: His father governed Nanyang under Emperor Ai.
units.literal: Yuan She's father in Emperor Ai's time was governor of Nanyang.

units.zh: 天下殷富，大郡二千石列官，賦斂送葬皆千萬以上，妻子通共受之，以定產業。
units.en: The empire was flush: great governors collected millions in funeral gifts, and families banked the windfall to build fortunes.
units.literal: The realm was rich; in great commanderies two-thousand-shi officials lined out offices; levies for sending off funerals all exceeded ten million; wives and children jointly received them to settle estates.

units.zh: 時又少行三年喪者。
units.en: Hardly anyone still kept three years of mourning.
units.literal: At that time there were again few who practiced the three-year mourning.

units.zh: 及涉父死，讓還南陽賻送，行喪塚廬三年，由是顯名京師。
units.en: When his father died he sent back the Nanyang condolence gold, mourned three years by the grave, and became famous in Chang'an.
units.literal: When Yuan She's father died, he declined and returned the Nanyang funeral gifts, observed mourning hut and tomb for three years, whereby he displayed his name in the capital.

units.zh: 禮畢，扶風謁請為議曹，衣冠慕之輻輳。
units.en: After mourning Fufeng named him a deliberation clerk, and every gentleman in the capital flocked to him.
units.literal: When the rites were finished, Fufeng invited him to serve as deliberation clerk; gentry admired him and crowded like spokes to a hub.

units.zh: 為大司徒史丹舉能治劇，為谷口令，時年二十餘。
units.en: Grand Minister of Education Shi Dan recommended him as capable of governing a difficult district, and Yuan She was appointed magistrate of Gukou while still in his twenties.
units.literal: Grand Minister of Education Shi Dan recommended him as able to govern a difficult county; he became magistrate of Gukou, at the time being over twenty.

units.zh: 谷口聞其名，不言而治。
units.en: Gukou obeyed his reputation before he issued a single order.
units.literal: Gukou heard his name and was governed without his speaking.

units.zh: 先是，涉季父為茂陵秦氏所殺，涉居谷口半歲所，自劾去官，欲報仇。
units.en: Years before, a Qin of Maoling had murdered his uncle; Yuan She quit Gukou after six months to hunt revenge.
units.literal: Earlier, Yuan She's father's younger brother had been killed by the Qin clan of Maoling; Yuan She dwelt at Gukou about half a year, impeached himself to leave office, wishing to avenge the wrong.

units.zh: 谷口豪桀為殺秦氏，亡命歲餘，逢赦出。
units.en: Local swordsmen slew the Qins for him; he hid a year, then walked free on a general amnesty.
units.literal: Gukou champions killed the Qin clan for him; he fled his life over a year, then met an amnesty and came out.

units.zh: 郡國諸豪及長安、五陵諸為氣節者皆歸慕之。
units.en: Every provincial bravo and Wuling gallant who cared about honor claimed him as hero.
units.literal: Champions of commanderies and kingdoms and those in Chang'an and the five mausoleum towns who cultivated integrity all turned to admire him.

units.zh: 涉遂傾身與相待，人無賢不肖闐門，在所閭里盡滿客。
units.en: He threw his doors open to saint and scoundrel alike until every lane he touched overflowed with clients.
units.literal: Thereupon he bent his body to treat them as equals; people whether worthy or not thronged his gate; in every ward where he stayed guests filled the lanes.

units.zh: 或譏涉曰：「子本吏二千石之世，結髮自修，以行喪推財禮讓為名，正復讎取仇，猶不失仁義，何故遂自放縱，為輕俠之徒乎？」
units.en: A critic said, "You were born to office, built a name on refusing gifts and keeping mourning—even blood feud could stay righteous—so why slide into alley-knight swagger?"
units.literal: Someone ridiculed Yuan She, saying: "You are from a two-thousand-shi clerk lineage, since tying the hair you have cultivated yourself, taking declining funeral wealth and yielding in ritual as your name—even if you avenged wrong and took enemies, you would still not lose benevolence and rightness—why then do you abandon yourself to license and become a follower of reckless knights?"

units.zh: 涉應曰：「子獨不見家人寡婦邪？
units.en: Yuan She shot back, "Have you never seen a household widow?
units.literal: Yuan She replied: "Have you alone not seen a household widow?

units.zh: 始自約敕之時，意乃慕宋伯姬及陳孝婦，不幸一為盜賊所污，遂行淫失，知其非禮，然不能自還。
units.en: At first she means to emulate Lady Bo Ji of Song and the filial wife of Chen; once defiled by bandits, she falls into debauchery, knows it is wrong, yet cannot turn back.
units.literal: At first, in the time of self-restraint, her intent then admired Lady Bo Ji of Song and the filial wife of Chen; unluckily once defiled by robbers, she then practiced debauchery and loss, knowing it was not ritual, yet could not return herself.

units.zh: 吾猶此矣！」
units.en: I am that widow."
units.literal: I am still like this!"

units.zh: 涉自以為前讓南陽賻送，身得其名，而令先人墳墓儉約，非孝也。
units.en: He decided that refusing Nanyang gold had bought him fame at the cost of shabby ancestral tombs—unfilial after all.
units.literal: He himself thought that earlier he had declined Nanyang funeral gifts and personally gained the name, yet caused his ancestors' graves to be meager—not filial.

units.zh: 乃大治起塚捨，周閣重門。
units.en: So he raised a mansion-tomb with ringed galleries and doubled gates.
units.literal: Thereupon he greatly built up tomb lodges, surrounding pavilions and double gates.

units.zh: 初，武帝時，京兆尹曹氏葬茂陵，民謂其道為京兆仟，涉慕之，乃買地開道，立表署曰南陽仟，人不肯從，謂之原氏仟。
units.en: Emperor Wu's Governor Cao had left a "Metropolitan Thousand" funeral avenue at Maoling; Yuan She copied the stunt, labeled his "Nanyang Thousand," but locals dubbed it the Yuan family lane.
units.literal: At first, in Emperor Wu's time, Metropolitan Governor Cao was buried at Maoling; the people called his road Metropolitan Thousand; Yuan She admired this, bought land, opened a road, set a marker inscribed Nanyang Thousand; people would not follow and called it Yuan Clan Thousand.

units.zh: 費用皆仰富人長者，然身衣服車馬才具，妻子內困。
units.en: Rich friends paid the bills while he dressed plain and kept his household short.
units.literal: Expenses all looked up to rich men and elders, yet his own clothes, carriages, and gear were modest; wife and children were inwardly pressed.

units.zh: 專以振施貧窮赴人之急為務。
units.en: His mission was feeding the hungry and answering every midnight plea.
units.literal: He devoted himself solely to relieving the poor and rushing to others' emergencies as his task.

units.zh: 人嘗置酒請涉，涉入里門，客有道涉所知母病避疾在裡宅者。
units.en: Someone once invited Yuan She to a banquet. As he entered the ward gate, a guest told him that the mother of a family he knew was ill and had moved to a house within the ward in hopes of escaping the sickness.
units.literal: Someone once laid out wine and invited Yuan She. As She entered the ward gate, a guest told him that the mother of a family he knew was ill and had moved to a house within the ward in hopes of escaping the sickness.

units.zh: 涉即往候，叩門。
units.en: He turned aside at once and knocked at her door.
units.literal: Yuan She immediately went to wait on her and knocked at the gate.

units.zh: 家哭，涉因入吊，問以喪事。
units.en: He found the house in tears, stepped in to mourn, and asked what the burial needed.
units.literal: The household was weeping; Yuan She therefore entered to condole and asked about funeral affairs.

units.zh: 家無所有，涉曰：「但潔掃除沐浴，待涉。」
units.en: They owned nothing; Yuan She said, "Scrub the rooms, wash the body, and wait for me."
units.literal: The household had nothing; Yuan She said: "Only sweep clean, bathe, and wait for me."

units.zh: 還至主人，對賓客歎息曰：「人親臥地不收，涉何心鄉此！
units.en: Back at the party he told the crowd, "A mother lies unburied—how can I swallow your wine!
units.literal: Returning to the host, he sighed to the guests: "With a parent lying on the ground unburied, how could I have heart for this feast!

units.zh: 願撤去酒食。」
units.en: Clear the table."
units.literal: I wish to remove the wine and food."

units.zh: 賓客爭問所當得，涉乃側席而坐，削牘為疏，具記衣被棺木，下至飯含之物，分付諸客。
units.en: Guests pressed for tasks; he sat, cut a tally sheet, and assigned shroud, coffin, even grave goods to each man.
units.literal: Guests vied to ask what should be obtained; Yuan She then sat sideways on the mat, shaved a slip into a list, fully noting shrouds, coffin wood, down to mouth-fill objects, assigning each to guests.

units.zh: 諸客奔走市買，至日昳皆會。
units.en: They scattered to the markets and reassembled by dusk with every item.
units.literal: The guests ran to the market to buy; by late afternoon all had assembled.

units.zh: 涉親閱視已，謂主人：「願受賜矣。」
units.en: He checked the haul and told the host, "Now I will take your cup."
units.literal: Yuan She personally inspected it and said to the host: "I wish to receive your gift."

units.zh: 既共飲食，涉獨不飽，乃載棺物，從賓客往至喪家，為棺斂勞徠畢葬。
units.en: He barely touched food, then convoyed the goods to the dead woman's house and stayed until she was sealed in the earth.
units.literal: Having together eaten and drunk, Yuan She alone did not eat his fill; then he loaded the coffin goods and, following guests, went to the mourning house, completing encoffining, labor, and burial.

units.zh: 其周急待人如此。
units.en: That was how he met emergencies.
units.literal: His relieving urgency and treating people were like this.

units.zh: 後人有毀涉者曰「奸人之雄也」，喪家子即時刺殺言者。
units.en: Later someone who slandered Yuan She said he was "champion of villains"; the son of the mourning house immediately stabbed and killed the speaker.
units.literal: Later someone who slandered Yuan She said he was "champion of villains"; the son of the mourning house immediately stabbed and killed the speaker.

units.zh: 賓客多犯法，罪過數上聞。
units.en: His followers broke laws until reports stacked up at court.
units.literal: Guests often violated the law; crimes and faults repeatedly were heard above.

units.zh: 王莽數收系欲殺，輒復赦出之。
units.en: Wang Mang jailed him again and again, then pardoned him every time.
units.literal: Wang Mang repeatedly seized and bound him wishing to kill, yet each time again amnestied and released him.

units.zh: 涉懼，求為卿府掾史，欲以避客。
units.en: He took a clerkship to dodge his mob of hangers-on.
units.literal: Yuan She feared and sought to become clerk in a minister's mansion, wishing thereby to avoid clients.

units.zh: 文母太后喪時，守復土校尉。
units.en: At Empress Dowager Wenmu's funeral, he served as colonel in charge of the burial works.
units.literal: At the funeral of the Literary Mother Empress Dowager, he served as colonel of the earth-returning work.

units.zh: 已為中郎，後免官。
units.en: He rose to gentleman of the palace, then lost the post.
units.literal: Later he became palace gentleman, then was dismissed.

units.zh: 涉欲上塚，不欲會賓客，密獨與故人期會。
units.en: He wanted a quiet grave visit and set secret rendezvous with old friends only.
units.literal: Yuan She wished to visit the tombs and did not want to meet guests; secretly he alone made appointments with old friends.

units.zh: 涉單車驅上茂陵，投暮，入其裡宅，因自匿不見人。
units.en: He raced alone to Maoling, slipped into his lane house at dusk, and hid.
units.literal: Yuan She drove a single cart hastening up to Maoling, threw himself at dusk into his ward house, and hid himself, seeing no one.

units.zh: 遣奴至市買肉，奴乘涉氣與屠爭言，斫傷屠者，亡。
units.en: He sent a slave for meat; the man picked a fight with a butcher, cut him, and bolted.
units.literal: He sent a slave to the market to buy meat; the slave, riding on Yuan She's temper, quarreled in words with a butcher, hacked and wounded the butcher, and fled.

units.zh: 是時，茂陵守令尹公新視事，涉未謁也，聞之大怒。
units.en: The new Maoling prefect Yin had not been visited; when he heard, he raged.
units.literal: At this time Prefect Yin of Maoling had newly taken office; Yuan She had not yet called on him; hearing of it he was greatly angry.

units.zh: 知涉名豪，欲以示眾厲俗，遣兩吏脅守涉。
units.en: Knowing Yuan She's fame, Yin posted two bailiffs on him to teach the town a lesson.
units.literal: Knowing Yuan She was a famous champion, he wished thereby to show the multitude and harden custom, and sent two clerks to coerce and guard Yuan She.

units.zh: 至日中，奴不出，吏欲便殺涉去。
units.en: Noon passed with no slave; the bailiffs threatened to execute Yuan She instead.
units.literal: By midday the slave had not appeared; the clerks wished on the spot to kill Yuan She and leave.

units.zh: 涉迫窘不知所為。
units.en: Yuan She was cornered.
units.literal: Yuan She was pressed and embarrassed, not knowing what to do.

units.zh: 會涉所與期上塚者車數十乘到，皆諸豪也，共說尹公。
units.en: Dozens of chariots of his grave-appointment allies roared in and pleaded with Yin.
units.literal: It happened that several tens of chariots of those Yuan She had appointed to meet for tomb visit arrived; all were champions and together remonstrated Prefect Yin.

units.zh: 尹公不聽，諸豪則曰：「原巨先奴犯法不得，使肉袒自縛，箭貫耳，詣廷門謝罪，於君威亦足矣。」
units.en: Yin refused; they offered, "Since the guilty slave cannot be caught, let Yuan She strip, bind himself, thread his ear with an arrow, and kowtow at your gate—that should satisfy your authority."
units.literal: Yin would not listen; the champions then said: "Since the offending slave cannot be caught, have Yuan She bare his torso, bind himself, run an arrow through his ear, and come to the court gate to apologize for his crime; for your authority that would also be enough."

units.zh: 尹公許之。
units.en: Yin agreed.
units.literal: Yin granted it.

units.zh: 涉如言謝，復服遣去。
units.en: Yuan She did the ritual penance and walked free.
units.literal: Yuan She apologized as spoken, was again clothed and sent away.

units.zh: 初，涉與新豐富人祁太伯為友，太伯同母弟王游公素嫉涉，時為縣門下掾，說尹公曰：「君以守令辱原涉如是，一旦真令至，君復單車歸為府吏，涉刺客如雲，殺人皆不知主名，可為寒心。
units.en: Yuan She had befriended Qi Taibo, a wealthy man of Xinfeng. Taibo's younger maternal half brother, Wang Yougong, had always resented Yuan She and was then a clerk in the county office. He told Yin, "As acting magistrate, you have humiliated Yuan She. Once the permanent magistrate arrives, you will return alone by cart to your old post as a commandery clerk. Yuan She's assassins are as numerous as clouds, and when they kill, no one ever knows who ordered it. The thought should chill you.
units.literal: Yuan She had befriended Qi Taibo, a wealthy man of Xinfeng. Taibo's younger maternal half brother, Wang Yougong, had long resented She and was then a clerk in the county office. He told Yin: "As acting magistrate, you have humiliated Yuan She in this way. Once the permanent magistrate arrives, you will return alone by cart to serve as a commandery clerk.
